summary: Today's health-tech news reflects significant activity across drug development, healthcare delivery infrastructure, and regulatory advances. In biotech financing, multiple companies secured substantial funding to advance novel therapies: City Therapeutics raised $200 million for RNA interference drugs targeting tissues beyond the liver, Iambic Therapeutics closed a $150 million IPO for AI-driven cancer drug discovery, and TRexBio brought in $116 million to develop immune-regulating therapeutics. Separately, Roche invested $100 million in an obesity treatment targeting ALK7, joining a competitive field that includes GSK and Arrowhead. On the AI and software side, Epic announced a prescription price comparison tool launching in summer 2027, while Teladoc Health added contactless vitals monitoring and ambient AI scribing to its virtual care platform, and multiple vendors like Healthleap and Vitalize secured funding to automate hospital workflows and improve patient screening. The regulatory landscape saw approvals for Happy Health's cuffless blood pressure monitoring ring and Asahi Kasei's Hovilpri herpes treatment, alongside FDA draft guidance on surgical robotics testing. Broader industry concerns also surfaced, including a Trilliant Health report highlighting how misaligned incentives are driving up costs and workforce shortages, while commentators emphasized the need to redesign primary care access and ensure accountability when AI flags clinical risks.
